degrees.field: Data science, biostatistics and college teaching
degrees.note: Non-credit courses from Johns Hopkins on Coursera, taken while on the faculty.

courses.title: Doctoral research and dissertation
courses.subject: dissertation
courses.description: Research units taken every term from spring 2008 through fall 2012 while working on the dissertation, Leadership Development in Core-Periphery Organizations, which completed the PhD in Industrial Administration at the Tepper School.
courses.materials_note: Listed on the transcript as research units each term, spring 2008 to fall 2012.

courses.title: Doctoral Seminar on Groups in Organizations
courses.subject: org-behavior
courses.description: A seminar on the core questions of research on groups at work. Students read and question the key studies, critique two assigned articles in writing, and pair up to describe the basic features of a real, ongoing work group, with the aim of spotting gaps in the literature and framing new research problems.

courses.title: Econometric Theory and Methods II
courses.subject: statistics
courses.description: The second PhD econometrics course at Heinz College, built on Wooldridge's Econometric Analysis of Cross Section and Panel Data. It opens with a review of maximum likelihood and M-estimators and moves into discrete outcome models and other microeconometric methods, with homework in Stata and R.

courses.title: Structural Equation Modeling (Psyed 3417)
courses.subject: statistics
courses.description: Taken at the University of Pittsburgh through cross-registration. The course reviews matrix algebra, covariance algebra, regression and factor analysis, then works through path analysis, confirmatory factor analysis, general SEM, mediation and moderation, latent growth curves and multigroup models, ending in an APA-style term paper that uses SEM.

courses.title: Workshop in Behavioral Research II
courses.subject: research
courses.instructor: Rosalind Chow and Anita Williams Woolley
courses.description: Second half of a year-long, learn-by-doing research workshop. Every other week two students present work in progress and the rest of the group serves as discussants, so the content follows the research interests of the people in the room rather than a fixed reading list.

courses.title: Workshop in Behavioral Research I
courses.subject: research
courses.instructor: Rosalind Chow and Anita Williams Woolley
courses.description: First half of a year-long research workshop that teaches the process of doing research by doing it. Students bring their own nascent projects, send readings ahead, present for half a session, and act as constructive discussants for each other's work.

courses.title: Graduate Reading and Research
courses.subject: research
courses.description: Independent summer reading and research for doctoral students, done with a faculty adviser rather than in a classroom. It typically supports a student's own research project between the coursework years.

courses.title: Advanced Topics: Hierarchical Linear Modeling (PSYED 3486)
courses.subject: statistics
courses.description: Taken at the University of Pittsburgh's School of Education through cross-registration. An introduction to hierarchical models for continuous and discrete outcomes, used when observations are clustered (students in classes, people in teams) and cannot be treated as independent. The main text was Raudenbush and Bryk's Hierarchical Linear Models.

courses.title: Intermediate Social Network Methodology
courses.subject: social-networks
courses.description: A follow-on to the fundamentals course that charts newer territory in network analysis. Analysis moves from UCINET to the social network packages in R, with a weekly hands-on exercise, student presentations of homework results, and a final exam built around analyzing a network.
courses.materials_note: The syllabus in the folder lists the course as 90-919; the transcript records it as 90-916.

courses.title: Introduction to Econometric Theory
courses.subject: statistics
courses.description: The first PhD econometrics course at Heinz College, taught from Wooldridge's Introductory Econometrics with Greene as a supplement. It covers the linear regression model and its assumptions, estimation and inference, through six problem sets, a midterm and a cumulative final.

courses.title: Organizational Learning
courses.subject: org-behavior
courses.description: A doctoral mini on how organizations learn: routines, knowledge transfer, and learning from experience, starting from classics such as Levitt and March. Students write short critiques of three papers and present them, alongside active class discussion.

courses.title: Applied Machine Learning (Machine Learning in Practice)
courses.subject: machine-learning
courses.description: A practical machine learning course cross-listed in HCII and LTI. It covers decision trees, rule-based classification, support vector machines, Bayesian networks and clustering, with weekly experiments in the Weka and TagHelper toolkits and a term project applying machine learning to a problem of the student's choice.

courses.title: Computer Supported Cooperative Work: Online Communities
courses.subject: web
courses.description: A research seminar on analyzing and designing online communities. Weekly topics ran from metaphors for online groups through bringing newcomers on board, building commitment, encouraging contribution, regulating behavior and coordination, to starting a new community, with a term project presented midway.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Social Network Methodology
courses.subject: social-networks
courses.description: A PhD seminar on the core methods of social network analysis using UCINET and Wasserman and Faust. Topics began with graph theory and matrix algebra and moved through power and centrality and related measures, with weekly data homework done in small groups and presented in class.

courses.title: Doctoral Seminar in Information Systems IV
courses.subject: infosys
courses.description: A seminar on the economics of information, networks and technology, using economic theory to study how information and technology shape organizations and markets. Students wrote short memos before most classes, led part of a discussion, and finished with a survey or research paper.

courses.title: Seminar in Information Systems III
courses.subject: infosys
courses.description: A doctoral information systems seminar with weekly readings and a research project. Ben's project studied group influences in peer-to-peer lending markets, using the borrower and lender groups on Prosper as the research setting.

courses.title: Research Methods for Behavioral Science
courses.subject: research
courses.description: A hands-on methods course for organizational behavior. The folder holds interview transcripts and critiques from paired interview projects, an observation exercise, and a reading list running from mediators and moderators to writing survey questions and assessing reliability.

courses.title: Seminar in Organizational Theory II
courses.subject: org-behavior
courses.description: The spring research seminar for first-year OB doctoral students, built around guest faculty talking about their own research and careers. Recurring themes were hard work and luck, learning from setbacks, what makes a good doctoral student, and how good researchers innovate on methods as well as theory.
courses.materials_note: My folder calls this class OB Research II, and my reflection paper is dated May 2008, the only spring OB seminar on the transcript.

courses.title: Foundations of Organizational Behavior
courses.subject: org-behavior
courses.description: Taken at the University of Pittsburgh through cross-registration. A doctoral foundations course in organizational behavior, covering how individuals and groups think, feel and act at work, and the research traditions behind those ideas.

courses.title: Knowledge Management Systems (BMIS 3021)
courses.subject: infosys
courses.description: Taken at Pitt's Katz Graduate School through cross-registration. A seminar on knowledge management and organizational learning, from tacit knowledge and exploration versus exploitation to knowledge management systems. Students wrote a research proposal and an essay on a debate in the field.

courses.title: Doctoral Seminar in Information Systems II
courses.subject: infosys
courses.description: A doctoral information systems seminar built on paper summary reports and a final paper. Ben's summaries covered open innovation, the long tail, information transparency in B2B markets, and organizational architecture in IT, and his final paper looked at how editors become administrators of Wikipedia.

courses.title: Seminar in Information Systems I
courses.subject: infosys
courses.description: The first doctoral IS seminar, organized around two questions: what is IS research, and how do we do it? It teaches by example and by doing, with weekly readings drawn largely from the instructor's own work on the business value of information technology.

courses.title: Seminar in Organizational Behavior (Macro)
courses.subject: org-behavior
courses.description: The macro side of the first-year doctoral seminar, focused on organization theory. It started with what makes a good theory, then covered population ecology and organizational learning, with written reviews of assigned papers. My final paper and talk looked at routines and knowledge transfer in open source software projects.
courses.materials_note: Both Fall 2007 seminars carry the same title on the transcript. My papers show one was micro and one macro, but not which course number was which.

courses.title: Seminar in Organizational Behavior (Micro)
courses.subject: org-behavior
courses.description: The micro side of the first-year doctoral seminar in organizational behavior. It opened by asking what OB is and how the field has changed, then worked through weekly readings on how people think and act at work. My papers were a critical review of research on identity and attachment at work, and a final paper and talk on role theory and role transitions.
courses.materials_note: Both Fall 2007 seminars carry the same title on the transcript. My papers show one was micro and one macro, but not which course number was which.

courses.title: Design and Analysis of Psychological Experiments
courses.subject: statistics
courses.description: A graduate statistics course on designing experiments and analyzing their results, covering analysis of variance, factorial designs and related methods, with weekly homework, computer labs in SPSS and exams.
courses.materials_note: The Drive folder is named Ed Psych 710.

courses.title: Multivariate Analysis
courses.subject: statistics
courses.description: Statistical tests framed as model comparisons, from regression and ANCOVA through multiple predictors, partial correlation and dummy coding, then matrix algebra, multivariate multiple regression, canonical correlation, MANOVA and discriminant functions. The course ran with two midterms and SPSS exercises.
courses.materials_note: The syllabus in the folder is a 2005 version of the same course.

courses.title: Reading and Research: Operations and Information Management
courses.subject: research
courses.description: Independent reading and research. This term's folder holds successive drafts of a paper on group efficacy and trust in virtual teams, prepared for the AMCIS conference, with research models and notes.
courses.materials_note: One Reading and Research folder covers both 799 courses this term.

courses.title: Reading and Research: Management
courses.subject: research
courses.description: Independent reading and research in management, taken alongside the OTM reading course in the final MBA semester while preparing for doctoral study. It shares a folder with the virtual teams paper.
courses.materials_note: One Reading and Research folder covers both 799 courses this term.

courses.title: Topic: Technology Entrepreneurship
courses.subject: entrepreneurship
courses.description: A research-oriented seminar organized by a long reading list: foundations of entrepreneurship from Schumpeter's creative destruction to Aldrich's Organizations Evolving, then entrepreneurs and entrepreneurial teams and later topics. Ben's folder holds a research proposal on open source communities as technology brokers.

courses.title: Analysis and Design of Computer-Based Systems
courses.subject: systems
courses.description: Object-oriented systems analysis and design: the analyst's role across the systems development life cycle, use cases turned into conceptual data models, sequence diagrams and design classes, CASE tools, and a semester-long development project for a local organization. Text: George, Batra, Valacich and Hoffer.

courses.title: PhD Communication for Dissertators
courses.subject: speech
courses.description: A one-credit communication course in the business PhD sequence, focused on presenting research. Ben's folder holds his presentation on virtual teams.

courses.title: Ethics, Integrity and Society
courses.subject: ethics
courses.description: A short required MBA course on ethics and integrity in business. The final project paired a personal goals statement with self-assessments, including a leadership and conflict resolution style assessment.

courses.title: Models for Event History Analysis
courses.subject: statistics
courses.description: A graduate sociology methods course on event history, or survival, analysis: life tables with and without censoring and the models that follow from them, taught with lecture notes and Stata data files.
courses.materials_note: The Drive folder is named Math Stats.

courses.title: Reading and Research: Operations and Information Management
courses.subject: research
courses.description: Independent reading and research in information systems. The folder gathers readings on design science and experimental research in IS, a virtual teams research thread, an ICIS paper template and a PhD application plan.

courses.title: Business Strategy
courses.subject: strategy
courses.description: The MBA core strategy course, taught through textbook chapters and cases. The folder holds case work on Ryanair, US Airways and Yum, a TQM unit, and readings such as the Intel and AMD race to quad-core.

courses.title: Information Security Management: Technology and Strategy
courses.subject: security
courses.description: Information security as a management problem: security in the enterprise, threat modeling, and the risks of IT outsourcing. The folder holds lectures, a threat modeling example, an outsourcing project and a final project on how secure IT outsourcing is.

courses.title: Computer-Based Data Management
courses.subject: databases
courses.description: Database design and management from the database environment and levels of data representation through the design life cycle, conceptual data modeling with the E-R model, class and subclass relationships and user-view modeling. Homework included the Pine Valley case and a conceptual and database design project.

courses.title: Economics for Managers
courses.subject: economics
courses.description: Managerial macroeconomics in a global setting: globalization and the closed-economy benchmark, comparative advantage and trade in goods and services, trade in capital and the balance of payments, trade policy, and money, inflation, interest rates and exchange rates in the long run.

courses.title: Operations Management
courses.subject: operations
courses.description: The MBA core in operations: process analysis, capacity, quality and delivery performance. Ben's team final project analyzed a company's plan to improve delivery reliability, with capacity utilization spreadsheets and a case presentation.

courses.title: Managing Behavior in Organizations (Motivation and Leadership)
courses.subject: org-behavior
courses.description: The MBA course on motivation and leadership. It combined required readings with case presentations, a career goal-setting analysis, a leadership style analysis, and a final group project with a write-up and presentation.

courses.title: Business Information Consulting
courses.subject: consulting
courses.description: Critical thinking and consulting skills for ambiguous business problems: client development and contracting, problem identification, planning and implementing a course of action, and evaluating the engagement, while extending accounting expertise into strategy. It ended in a consulting capstone.

courses.title: Professional Perspectives (II)
courses.subject: career
courses.description: The second semester of the MBA professional development sequence. Materials include a decision making class with organizational culture surveys and a technology article for discussion.

courses.title: Data Analysis and Decision Making
courses.subject: statistics
courses.description: The MBA core statistics course: organizing and summarizing data, probability, common distributions and the decision tools built on them, taught through lecture notes, lab files and assignments.

courses.title: Marketing Management
courses.subject: marketing
courses.description: A survey of the key decisions in a firm's marketing program: product, pricing, distribution channels and promotion, and how they fit together, plus models for analyzing customers and competitors. Cases in the folder include the Beetle, Population Services and Sealed Air.

courses.title: Technology of Computer-Based Business Systems
courses.subject: infosys
courses.description: An introduction to the technology behind business information systems, covering hardware, software, networks and data, with lecture notes, labs, code resources and assignments.

courses.title: Introduction to Financial Management
courses.subject: finance
courses.description: The MBA core corporate finance course, following Ross, Westerfield and Jaffe's Corporate Finance: time value of money, valuation and capital budgeting, through lecture notes, problem sets, articles, exams and a group project on Exxon Mobil.

courses.title: Financial Accounting
courses.subject: accounting
courses.description: The MBA core in financial accounting: accrual accounting, the main financial statements and how to read them, taught in modules with homework, quizzes and a company analysis of Exxon Mobil.

courses.title: Professional Perspectives (I)
courses.subject: career
courses.description: The first semester of the MBA professional development sequence: behavioral interviewing, competencies and networking, with the program's recruiting tools.

courses.title: Introduction to Philosophy
courses.subject: ethics
courses.description: An introduction to the central questions of philosophy, such as knowledge, mind, God and ethics, through classic and modern readings. It counted toward the general education humanities requirement.

courses.title: Introduction to Abstract Algebra
courses.subject: math
courses.description: An introduction to algebraic structures, mainly groups and rings, with proofs about subgroups, homomorphisms and quotient structures.

courses.title: Actuarial Mathematics
courses.subject: probability
courses.description: The mathematics of insurance and annuities: interest theory, survival models and life tables, and the pricing of life contingent payments.

courses.title: Mathematical Statistics
courses.subject: statistics
courses.description: The theory behind statistical inference, following probability theory: sampling distributions, point and interval estimation, and hypothesis testing.

courses.title: Administrative Policy (Strategic Management)
courses.subject: strategy
courses.description: Known to most as strategic management, this course took a senior management view of the firm across seven online modules, each with an audio lecture, a case and discussion, a graded exercise and a self-assessment, using Thompson and Strickland's Strategic Management.

courses.title: Network Engineering
courses.subject: networks
courses.description: Data communications and networking for business systems: media such as copper and fiber, digital transmission, long-distance digital connection technologies, and network design. The folder holds a class presentation, the midterm and the final.

courses.title: Probability Theory
courses.subject: probability
courses.description: Calculus-based probability: random variables, distributions, expectation and limit theorems. Ben's papers applied it to The Price Is Right and to a classroom experiment on how a Hershey's Kiss lands.

courses.title: Introduction to Analysis (Introduction to Proof)
courses.subject: math
courses.description: A transition to higher mathematics: logic, sets and functions, methods of proof, and a rigorous look at sequences, limits and the real numbers.

courses.title: Business Finance
courses.subject: finance
courses.description: The core business finance course: time value of money, risk and return, valuation and capital budgeting, worked through spreadsheet assignments.

courses.title: Business Communication
courses.subject: writing
courses.description: Writing for business: memos, letters, reports and proposals, with attention to audience and tone. Ben's team wrote an e-learning recommendation report and a proposal to improve career services use on campus.

courses.title: Career Information
courses.subject: career
courses.description: A one-credit course on career planning and the job search: exploring career paths, résumés and interviewing.

courses.title: Ethnic Politics
courses.subject: politics
courses.description: American ethnic and immigrant politics, read through models such as the civic culture model and applied to German, Irish and Mexican immigration. Ben's group presented on the history and future of Mexican immigration.

courses.title: Systems Analysis and Design 2
courses.subject: systems
courses.description: Second half of the systems analysis and design sequence. The team carried a real client project for a campus department from analysis into design iterations, a design model and an implementation plan, with project plans along the way.
courses.materials_note: A second copy sits in the SAD backup folder.

courses.title: Web Development 2
courses.subject: web
courses.description: Server-side Java web development: servlets and JSP on Tomcat, request headers, cookies and session tracking, and database access with JDBC against SQL Server.
courses.materials_note: More code from this course is in the web2 and ServletDevel folders.

courses.title: Matrices and Linear Algebra
courses.subject: math
courses.description: Systems of linear equations, matrices and determinants, vector spaces, linear transformations, and eigenvalues and eigenvectors.

courses.title: Business and Commercial Law
courses.subject: law
courses.description: The legal environment of business, centered on contracts, along with torts, agency, sales and business organizations. The folder holds a contract drafting exercise.

courses.title: Systems Analysis and Design 1
courses.subject: systems
courses.description: First half of the systems analysis and design sequence, run as a team project for a real campus client: problem statement, feasibility assessment, use cases, and inception and elaboration presentations, modeled in Rational Rose.

courses.title: Web Development 1
courses.subject: web
courses.description: An introduction to building web sites and web applications, from HTML to server-side scripting with Active Server Pages.

courses.title: Discrete Mathematics
courses.subject: math
courses.description: Logic, sets, relations and functions, induction, counting, recurrences and graphs: the mathematics behind computer science.

courses.title: Principles of Marketing
courses.subject: marketing
courses.description: The introductory marketing course: consumer behavior, segmentation and targeting, and the marketing mix of product, price, place and promotion.

courses.title: Operations Management
courses.subject: operations
courses.description: Managing how goods and services are produced. Ben's notes cover total quality management, project management, just-in-time and lean manufacturing, inventory systems and operations scheduling.

courses.title: Business Statistics I
courses.subject: statistics
courses.description: Descriptive statistics, probability, sampling distributions, estimation and hypothesis testing for business, practiced in Excel.
courses.materials_note: Links to a homework spreadsheet; there is no course folder.

courses.title: Organizational Behavior
courses.subject: org-behavior
courses.description: Individual and group behavior at work: perception, motivation, teams, leadership, communication and organizational culture.

courses.title: World of Ideas
courses.subject: ethics
courses.description: An upper-level general education humanities course on ideas that shaped the world. Ben's essays took on the American Dream, the wealth of nations, class, religion, and Zen and peace negotiations.

courses.title: Personal Health and Fitness for Life
courses.subject: health
courses.description: A one-credit physical education course on lifelong fitness, exercise and wellness.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Speech
courses.subject: speech
courses.description: Public speaking basics: preparing, outlining and delivering informative and persuasive speeches. Ben's folder holds a persuasive speech on donating plasma, a group speech on advertising and a self evaluation.

courses.title: Concepts of COBOL with File Structures
courses.subject: programming
courses.description: Business programming in COBOL, with sequential and relative file structures, sorting and report generation, built in the Fujitsu COBOL environment.

courses.title: Calculus and Analytic Geometry III
courses.subject: math
courses.description: Multivariable calculus: vectors, partial derivatives, multiple integrals and vector calculus.

courses.title: Economic Principles, Problems and Policies
courses.subject: economics
courses.description: The second semester of principles of economics, applying supply, demand and economic reasoning to national and policy questions.

courses.title: Managerial Accounting
courses.subject: accounting
courses.description: Accounting for decisions inside the firm: cost behavior, job and process costing, budgeting and standard costs, worked as spreadsheet problems.

courses.title: Concepts of Data Structures
courses.subject: programming
courses.description: Core data structures and the algorithms that use them: arrays, lists, stacks, queues, trees, searching and sorting.

courses.title: Calculus and Analytic Geometry II
courses.subject: math
courses.description: Integration techniques and applications, sequences and series, and parametric and polar curves.

courses.title: The Logic of Chess
courses.subject: chess
courses.description: A one-credit course using chess to practice logical and strategic reasoning.

courses.title: Accounting Concepts
courses.subject: accounting
courses.description: Introductory financial accounting: the accounting cycle, journal entries, worksheets and financial statements, practiced through weekly spreadsheet problems.

courses.title: Concepts of Programming
courses.subject: programming
courses.description: A first programming course for management computer systems majors: variables, control structures, procedures and problem solving in code.

courses.title: Calculus and Analytic Geometry I
courses.subject: math
courses.description: Limits, derivatives and their applications, and an introduction to integration.

courses.title: Individual and Society
courses.subject: psychology
courses.description: A general education social science course on how individuals and society shape each other. Ben's work includes a critical thinking project on a psychology article and essays tying Octavia Butler's Parable of the Sower to the news.
courses.materials_note: The Drive folder is named I&S Psych.

courses.title: World of the Arts
courses.subject: arts
courses.description: A general education survey of the visual and performing arts and how to look at, listen to and talk about them.

courses.title: Economic Principles, Problems and Policies
courses.subject: economics
courses.description: The first semester of principles of economics: scarcity, markets, supply and demand, and how households and firms make choices.

courses.title: Physical Science Foundations
courses.subject: science
courses.description: A general education laboratory course introducing the physical sciences through hands-on labs.

courses.title: Concepts of Database Systems
courses.subject: databases
courses.description: An introduction to database concepts: tables, keys, relationships and queries, built in Microsoft Access and SQL.
courses.materials_note: Best match: the Database Project 1 folder of Access databases and SQL.

courses.title: Finite Mathematics for Business and Social Sciences
courses.subject: math
courses.description: Linear equations and matrices, linear programming, the mathematics of finance, and basic probability for business applications.

courses.title: Freshman English (Honors)
courses.subject: writing
courses.description: The honors section of second-semester composition. Ben's research project, The Sermon of the Theatre, looked at religious drama from The Second Shepherds' Play to Marlowe's Doctor Faustus, alongside an advertisement analysis and notes on poems about suffering, change and death.

courses.title: Freshman English
courses.subject: writing
courses.description: First-semester college composition, credited as UW-Whitewater's English 101. Papers labelled CAPP Comp in Ben's high school folder suggest it was taken through CAPP, UW Oshkosh's high school partnership program.
courses.materials_note: Mixed folder: look for files that start with CAPP Comp.

courses.title: Biology (transfer elective)

courses.description: The opening course of the specialization. It sets up the tools used in the rest of it, R, RStudio, Git and GitHub, and the kinds of questions data scientists ask.

courses.title: University Teaching 101

courses.description: The basics of college teaching, from planning a course and writing objectives to active learning, using a learning management system, and assessment. The folder holds the course quizzes.
